correctness.rationale: From a+1=(t+1)(b+1), p is congruent to -2^b modulo the odd q, so the two odd factors are coprime and both exceed 1. The four odd parts 1,p,q,pq are distinct; complementation preserves the box and the two omitted pairs are disjoint (their entries have precisely these odd parts). With T=2^(a+1) and B=2^b, the box sum is 2B(T-1)(T-B), the omitted sum is 2B^2+Tp, and (T-1)(T-B)-B=Tp. The remaining sum is Tp(2B-1)=2N. If q=2^(b+1)-1 were a proper power, use a prime exponent r: for r=2, b+1=2 is immediate and b+1>=3 is impossible modulo 8; for odd r, (z^r+1)/(z+1) is odd and greater than 1, impossible for a divisor of a power of 2. The valuations of q survive in N, excluding all proper powers. Both positive factors in 2^a p increase strictly with a; log N=2(b+1)t log 2+O_b(1), and upper and lower cutoffs on t give the stated count. For b=1, p is coprime to 3 for every a>=2, so the same identity applies and v_3(N)=1. The supplied grid and row replay were inspected as finite regression evidence, not rerun or used for the infinite conclusions.
residual_risks: No maximality of the progression or claim about odd primitive examples follows.
